Qnami is a Swiss high‑tech company that develops and commercializes quantum sensing technology—using the principles of quantum mechanics to create extremely precise sensors and scientific instruments.

🔬 What Qnami Does

Quantum sensing: Qnami leverages the quantum properties of nitrogen‑vacancy (NV) centers—atomic‑scale defects in ultra‑pure diamond—to build sensors capable of measuring magnetic fields, electrical currents, temperature, and other physical quantities with extraordinarily high sensitivity and spatial resolution. These quantum sensors can detect signals at the nanoscale that traditional sensors cannot.

Scientific instruments:
• It produces quantum microscopes, most notably the ProteusQ system—one of the first commercially available scanning NV magnetometers. This instrument maps magnetic fields and material properties down to atomic scales, combining microscopy with quantum sensing.

• Qnami also offers diamond‑based probes (Quantilever™) and related software and analytics to support high‑precision measurement.

Applications: Its tools are used primarily in materials science, nanotechnology, semiconductor research, and life/earth sciences—for example, to study the magnetic properties of new materials, improve chip design, and explore phenomena that were previously unmeasurable.

Origins & focus: The company was founded in 2017 out of research at the University of Basel and positions itself as a leader in commercial quantum sensing, bridging cutting‑edge physics with real research and industrial applications.
